sentences.text: The type specimen represents a small reptile measuring exactly 75 cm in length.
Specimens of this animal lack pachyostosis, a condition where bones become unusually thick and heavy.
The genus was first formally described by Rieppel in 1989.
A second species, Serpianosaurus germanicus, was described and named by Cajus G. Diedrich in 2013.
There are 14 recorded fossil occurrences of Serpianosaurus known to science.
Sexual dimorphism in Serpianosaurus is indicated by differences in humeral size and shape between males and females.
Morphological evidence suggests Serpianosaurus is one of the most basal forms of sauropterygians.
Serpianosaurus belongs to the superorder Sauropterygia.
The animal is classified within the family Pachypleurosauridae.
The type species of Serpianosaurus is Serpianosaurus mirigiolensis.
Serpianosaurus, meaning "Serpiano lizard", lived during the Middle Triassic in Switzerland and Germany.
Fossils of Serpianosaurus mirigiolensis date to around 242 million years ago at the Anisian/Ladinian boundary.
Fossils of Serpianosaurus have been found in the middle Grenzbitumenzone, the oldest strata of Monte San Giorgio in Switzerland.
